flashcard_questions.q: What temperature range is called the danger zone?
How often can bacteria divide in ideal conditions?
What is the name for bacteria splitting into two identical cells?
Why does drying food stop bacteria multiplying?
flashcard_questions.a: Bacteria need moisture, and dried foods hold very little water.

flashcard_questions.q: Why can food carrying dangerous bacteria still look and smell normal?
flashcard_questions.a: Pathogenic bacteria do not change the appearance, smell or taste of food.
Enzymes in cut fruit or vegetables react with oxygen, turning the surface brown.

flashcard_questions.q: Which type of contamination covers hair, glass and plasters in food?
Which type of contamination comes from cleaning products or pesticides?

flashcard_questions.a: The transfer of harmful bacteria from one food or surface to another.

flashcard_questions.q: On which fridge shelf should raw meat be stored?
Which bacterium is the most common cause of food poisoning in the UK?
Which pathogen can still grow at fridge temperatures below 5°C?
What core temperature must food reach to be safely cooked?
How quickly should cooked food be cooled before refrigerating?
Which bacterium produces toxins in cooked rice that is reheated?

notes: 15 cards: 4 value/temperature cards (danger zone, 10-20 minutes, 75°C core, 90 minutes cooling), 4 process cards (drying, invisible pathogens, enzymic browning, cross-contamination), 3 pathogen-to-feature, 2 contamination-type, 2 practice cards. Dropped FATTOM, the four contamination types as a list, the chopping-board colour set and the five-signs-of-spoilage list as enumerations; two contamination types are kept as separately cued cards instead.
